subject: Re: Marketplace SKU conversion & seat-to-commit migration plan
messages:
From: Ava Brooks <ava.brooks@novuslabs.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novuslabs.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace SKU conversion & seat-to-commit migration plan

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the walk-through earlier. We reviewed the proposal and the leadership team wants to move ahead with converting our existing seat-based Marketplace listing into a committed-usage private offer. Main asks from Finance/Procurement: a clear SKU mapping (old seat SKUs -> new committed SKUs), a proposed billing cadence (we prefer quarterly tranches instead of lump-sum annual), and confirmation of SLA parity for the new offer.

Two risks we flagged: (1) how usage overage will be billed during the first 90 days of the new term while our consumption ramps, and (2) how tax/VAT will be handled for split invoices between our US and EU entities.

Can you share a migration plan and a sample private-offer DocuSign for review? We need internal sign-off by 9/22 to make the Oct 1 cutover.

Appreciate it — Ava
Ava Brooks
Head of Cloud Ops, Novus Labs
ava.brooks@novuslabs.com

---
Attachment: Novus-SKU-map-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 38 KB)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ava Brooks <ava.brooks@novuslabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU conversion & seat-to-commit migration plan

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear asks. I’ve attached a first-pass SKU mapping (same file you uploaded, annotated) and sketched a migration timeline that keeps you covered during the ramp. High-level notes:

- Mapping: We map seat SKUs to two committed tiers (Standard-commit, Peak-commit) to preserve price bands. See sheet "Mapping + Rationale."
- Billing cadence: We can structure the private offer into four quarterly invoices (Qtr tranches) that invoice in advance. Each tranche will be tied to a committed capacity bucket.
- Overages: For the first 90 days we recommend a temporary buffering policy: overage tokens are billed at an interim uplift (list price + 12%), with any measurable underrun/overrun reconciled at the end of the first quarter and applied to the next tranche. This avoids surprise clawbacks.
- SLA parity: Confirmed — same latency & uptime SLAs apply; we’ll add the private-offer SLA addendum.
- Tax: We’ll build a split-invoice flow and include tax tags per entity; legal will add the exact VAT language.

I’m looping in Ben (billing) and Kim (marketplace/legal) to finalize DocuSign and the private-offer asset. Ben / Kim — can you review the annotated SKU mapping and confirm the quarterly invoice flow and interim overage language? We should also include a DocuSign link so Novus can start routing for signatures today.

Next steps: I’ll have the private-offer draft + DocuSign envelope by end of day Monday (9/18) if we get alignment on the overage approach.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
Phone: (415) 555-0192

Attachment: Novus-SKU-map-v2.xlsx (annotated)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Marketplace SKU conversion & seat-to-commit migration plan

Monica / Kim — quick notes from billing/legal POV after a pass through the workbook: 

1) Quarterly advance invoicing is fine. We can set invoice windows to 30 days prior to each quarter start (e.g., invoice Sept 1 for Q4). That matches Novus' preference and helps cash flow smoothing.
2) Interim overage rate: +12% is a reasonable short-term approach. Recommend we cap the interim overage charge to 20% of the tranche value in any single month to avoid large spikes. Reconcile net overage vs committed quantity at quarter-end and issue a credit or additional invoice accordingly.
3) VAT / tax: Kim — we need a one-line reprieve in the DocuSign stating that split-invoice tax treatment is subject to customer's local tax authority; redlines will follow.

Jordan: can you create the private-offer envelope and include two acceptance options in DocuSign: (A) Quarterly-tranche private offer (preferred) and (B) Annual prepaid (fallback option)? That will speed legal sign-off downstream.

If we get sign-off today, we can have the DocuSign sent to Novus legal by EOD.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment referenced: Novus-MAP-summary-legal-9-17.pdf
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ava Brooks <ava.brooks@novuslabs.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@novuslabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Eli Navarro <eli.navarro@novuslabs.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace SKU conversion & seat-to-commit migration plan

Ava / team — good news: DocuSign envelope has been created with both acceptance choices (quarterly-tranche private offer + annual-prepaid fallback). I attached the summary legal memo and the annotated SKU map. Highlights for Novus review: 

- Billing: Four quarterly advance invoices; first invoice issued on Sept 30 to cover Oct–Dec tranche.
- Overages: Interim +12% rate with a monthly cap at 20% of tranche; quarter-end reconciliation credit/charge.
- SLA & Support: SLA addendum is included (no change in latency/uptime commitments).
- Tax: DocuSign includes a clause that splits invoices by entity; Novus legal to confirm VAT language.

Please use this DocuSign link to review and sign: https://www.docusign.net/recipient/details?envelopeId=9a2b-45271-c

If you prefer an annual prepaid instead, choose option B in the envelope — our system will generate the single invoice and apply the committed discount.

If Novus can sign by EOD 9/19 we’ll push the private offer to production and schedule the Oct 1 SKU swap window. If there are any legal redlines, please send them back to kimberly.park@redwood.com.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this over the finish line.

Best,
Monica
